questions.q: The half-lives of two radioactive nuclides $A$ and $B$ are 1 and $2 \mathrm{~min}$ respectively. Equal weights of $A$ and $B$ are taken separately and allowed to disintegrate for $4 \mathrm{~min}$. What will be the ratio of weights of $A$ and $B$ disintegrated?
questions.solution:
For, $A t_{1 / 2}=1 \mathrm{~min}\therefore$ part of $A$ remained after 4 minutes
$\text { (i.e., } 4 \text { half- life) will be }=\frac{1}{16}\therefore$ part of $A$ disintegrated in the same period $=\frac{15}{16}$
For $B, t_{1 / 2}=2 \mathrm{~min}\therefore$ Part of $B$ remained after 4 minutes (i.e., 2 half life)
$=\frac{1}{4}\therefore$ part of $B$ disintegrated in the same time $=\frac{3}{4}$
Hence, ratio of disintegrated weights of $A$ and
$B=\frac{15}{16}: \frac{3}{4}=15: 12=5: 4$

In the reaction$

It is a complex reaction because more then one steps are present.

The energy of activation for an uncatalysed reaction is 100 kJ mol-1. Presence of a catalyst lowers the energy of activation by 75%. The $\log_{1 0} \dfrac{{K}_{2}}{{K}_{1}}$ of the ratio of rate constant of catalysed and uncatalysed reactions at 27°C is?

Assume the frequency factor is same for both reactions. (Given 2.303 × 8.314 = 19.147)
questions.solution:
In absence of catalyst, ${K}_{1} = {Ae}^{- 1 0 0 / \text{RT}}$

In presence of catalyst ; ${K}_{2} = {Ae}^{- 2 5 / \text{RT}}$

$∴ \dfrac{{K}_{2}}{{K}_{1}} = e^{7 5 / \text{RT}} ⇒ \log_{\mathrm{e}} \dfrac{{K}_{2}}{{K}_{1}} = \dfrac{7 5}{\text{RT}}$

$⇒ \log_{1 0} \dfrac{{K}_{2}}{{K}_{1}} = \dfrac{7 5}{\text{2.303} \times \text{R} \times \text{T}}$

$⇒ \log_{1 0} \dfrac{{K}_{2}}{{K}_{1}} = \dfrac{7 5}{\text{2.303} \times \text{8.314} \times 1 {0}^{- 3} \times 3 0 0} = 13.057$

questions.q: The rate equation for a first order reaction is given by $[R]=[R]_0 e^{-k t}$. A straight line with positive slope is obtained by plotting. $[R]_0=$ initial concentration of reactant, $[R]=$ concentration of reactant at time, $t$
questions.solution: For the equation $[R]=[R]_0 e^{-k t}$ Taking log we get $\begin{array}{rlrl}$& \ln [R] & =-k t+\operatorname{in}[R]_0 \\ & \therefore & \ln $\frac{[R]}{[R]_0}$& =-k t \\ & & & \\ k & =$\frac{1}{t} \text { in } \frac{[R]_0}{[R]}$\\ k & =$\frac{2.303}{t} \log \frac{[R]_0}{[R]} \end{array}$When graph is ploted of $\log \frac{[R]_0}{[R]}$ against $t$, we get a straight line with positive slope $=\frac{k}{2.303}$.

After $20$ minutes from the start, the total pressure developed is found to be $350mmHg$ in place of initial pressure $200mmofHg$ of azomethane. The value of rate constant $k$ is:$

This problem is based on conceptual mixing of determination of partial pressure and rate constant, which can be solved as follows.

$\text{k} = \dfrac{2.303}{t} log \left(\dfrac{Pi}{Pt}\right)$

\left({CH}_{3}\right)2{N}_{2} \to {C}_{2}{H}_{6} + {N}_{2}$

$\$begin{cases}\text{t} =$0 \text{ and } 200 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } 0 \\ $\text{t} = \text{t}$ \text{ and } $\text{200-x}$ \text{ and } $\text{x}$ \text{ and } $\text{x}\end{cases}

Given, $200 - $\text{x} + \text{x} + \text{x} =$350$

\text{x} =$1 5 0$

\text{k} = \dfrac{\text{2.303}}{\text{t}}$log $\$left(\dfrac{2 0 0}{2 0 0 - 1 5 0}\right)

$\text{k} = $\dfrac{\text{2.303}}{2 0} \left(log $\dfrac{2 0 0}{5 0}\right)

\text{k} = \dfrac{\text{2.303}}{2 0} \times$2 log 2$

\text{k} = \dfrac{\text{2.303}}{2 0} \times$2 $\times \text{0.3010} = \dfrac{\text{0.693}}{1 0}

$= $\text{6.93} \times$1 {0}^{- 2} \min^{-1}$

Consider the following gaseous decomposition of ozone:

$2 {O}_{3} \left(\text{g}\right)⟶ 3 {O}_{2} \left(\text{g}\right). The observed rate law is \text{r} = \dfrac{- \text{d} \left[{O}_{3}\right]}{\text{dt}} = \dfrac{\text{k} {\left[{O}_{3}\right]}^{2}}{\left[{O}_{2}\right]}
If the above reaction occurs through the following mechanism:

\begin{cases}{O}_{3} \overset{K}{⇌} {O}_{2} +\text{O}$& \left(\text{fast equilibrium}\right)$\\ $\text{O} + {O}_{3} \overset{\text{k} 1}{⟶}$2 {O}_{2} & \left(\text{slow}\right)\end{cases}

Then, which of the following& relation is correct?

$

In Complex Reaction Rate law is defined by the slowest step. So According to slowest step Rate Law Expression can be represented as:

$\text{Rate law} = \text{r} = {k}_{1}\left[\text{O}\right]\left[{O}_{3}\right]\text{...........(1)}$

Now Intermediate term ie [O]~can never comes in Rate Law Expression.So to eliminate it,we apply Equilibrium constant Expression on Reversible Equation.

~ ~ $\text{K} = \left[{O}_{2}\right]\left[\text{O}\right]\left[{O}_{3}\right] . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 2 ) ( K = Equilibriumconstant ) \left[$O\right] = K \left[{O}_{3}\right]\left[{O}_{2}\right]

On Puting value of [O] in Equation $1$, we get

~ ~$⇒ $\text{r} = {k}_{1}\text{K} \left[{O}_{3}\right]2 \left[{O}_{2}\right]

\text{r} = \text{k}\left[{O}_{3}\rright]2\left[{O}_{2}\right]( \text{k} = {k}_{1}\text{K)}$

$

First-order reaction is the rate of reaction is proportional to the first power of the concentration of the reactant& $R$.

If we plot a graph between~log\left[{R}_{0}\right]\left[$R\right]$~Vs $t$, slope~$= $\dfrac{k}{2 . 303}.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: In collision theory, \(e^{-E_{\mathrm{n}} / R T}\) corresponds to the fraction of molecules that have energy equal or greater than \(E_a\)
The number of collisions of reacting molecules per second per unit volume of the reaction mixture is activated complex
Molecularity is the number of molecules involved in a complex reaction
A catalyst catalyses the non-spontaneous reaction
questions.solution: (a) In collision theory, \(e^{-E_a / R T}\) corresponds to the fraction of molecules that have energy equal to or greater than \(E_a\) (activation - energy) is the correct statement because it is in accordance with Arrhenius theory. (b) The number of collision of the reacting molecules per second per unit volume of the reaction mixture is activated complex is not a correct statement as activated complexes are formed during the reaction, which finally gives the product. (c) Molecularity is the number of molecules involved in a complex reaction. This is also not correct as molecularity is defined as: The number of reacting species taking part in a reaction, which must collide simultancously in order to bring out the reaction. (d) A catalyst, catalyses the non-spontaneous reaction. This is also not correct as a catalyst can catalyse the spontaneous as well as non-spontaneous reactions. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.q: For the following reaction of first-order ${N}_{2}{O}_{5} ( g ) \to 2{NO}_{2} ( g ) + 1 / 2{O}_{2} ( g )$, if the total pressure of the system after $20$ minutes is $220$ mm and after a very long time, total pressure is $400mm,$ then ${t}_{1 / 2}$ for the reaction is
questions.solution:
After a very long time, the reaction can be assumed to be completed.

Thus, for the given reaction,

$\begin{cases} & {N}_{2}{O}_{5} & \overset{}{→} & 2{NO}_{2} & + & \dfrac{1}{2}{O}_{2} \\ t = 0 & {P}_{0} & & 0 & & 0 \\ t = 20mins & {P}_{0} - p & & 2p & & \dfrac{p}{2} \\ t \to \infty & 0 & & 2{P}_{0} & & \dfrac{P0}{2}\end{cases}$

According to the question, after a very long time,

$2{P}_{0} + \dfrac{P0}{2} = 400 ⇒ \dfrac{5}{2}{P}_{0} = 400 ⇒ {P}_{0} = 160mm$

And, after $20$ minutes,

${P}_{0} - p + 2p + \dfrac{p}{2} = 220mm ⇒ 160 + \dfrac{3}{2}p = 220 ⇒ \dfrac{3}{2}p = 60 ⇒ p = 40mm$

Now, we know that,~$k = \dfrac{0 . 693}{t1 / 2}$

Applying the integrated rate law after $20$ mins of reactions,

$20 = \dfrac{2 . 303}{k}log\dfrac{160}{160 - 40} ⇒ 20 = \dfrac{2 . 303 \times {t}_{1 / 2}}{0 . 693}log\dfrac{160}{120} ⇒ \dfrac{20 \times 0 . 693}{2 . 303} = {t}_{1 / 2} \times log\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right) ⇒ {t}_{1 / 2} \approx \dfrac{6}{log\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)}$

questions.q: Why do we use the carbon dating to calculate the age of the fossil?
options: Rate of exchange of carbon between atmosphere and living is slower than decay of $C^{14}$.
It is not appropriate to use $C^{14}$dating to determine age.
Rate of exchange of $C^{14}$between atmosphere and living organism is so fast that an equilibrium is set up between the intake of $C^{14}$by organism and its exponential decay.
questions.solution:
It is clear from the ${3}^{rd}$paragraph, which states that in living organisms a dynamic equilibrium is established where by the ratio of $C^{14}$to $C^{12}$remains constant.

Hence,~$C^{14}$which decays into $N^{14}$is replenished by the production of new isotopes.

questions.q: The half-life periods of a first order reaction at $300 \mathrm{~K}$ and $400 \mathrm{~K}$ are $50 \mathrm{~s}$ and $10 \mathrm{~s}$ respectively. The activation energy of the reaction in $\mathrm{kJ} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ is $(\log 5=0.70)$
questions.solution: Given, For first order reaction, (i) half-life  \left(t_{1 / 2}\right)$ at temperature $300 \mathrm{~K}=50 \mathrm{~s}$ (ii) half-life  \left(t_{1 / 2}\right)$ at temperature $400 \mathrm{~K}=10 \mathrm{~s}\begin{aligned}$& \therefore \quad K_1(\text { at } 300 \mathrm{~$K})=\frac{0.693}{50}=0.014 \mathrm{~s}^{-1} \\  \text{ and }  \text { and } K_2(\text { at } 400 \mathrm{~$K})=\frac{0.693}{10}=0.07 \mathrm{~s}^{-1} \\ & \left.\qquad \because K=0.693 / t_{(1 / 2)} \text { for lst order reaction }\right] \end{aligned} where, $K_1$ and $K_2$ are rate constant at $300 \mathrm{~K}$ and $400 \mathrm{~K}$ respectively. Also, according to Arrhenius theory \log $\frac{K_2}{K_1}=\frac{E_a}{2.303 R}  \left[\frac{T_2-T_1}{T_1 \cdot T_2}\right]$where, $E_a=$ activation energy $\begin{aligned}$T_1 \text{ and } =\text { temperature }(300 \mathrm{~K}) \\ T_2 \text{ and } =\text { temperature }(400 \mathrm{~K}) \\ R \text{ and } =\operatorname{gas} \text { constant }\left(8.314 \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\right) \end{aligned} Thus, $\begin{aligned}$ \text{ and } \log $\frac{0.07}{0.014}=\frac{E_a}{2.303 \times 8.314}  \left[\frac{400-300}{400 \times 300}\right]$\\ & \text { or, } \quad \log $5=\frac{E_a}{2.303 \times 8.314}  \left[\frac{100}{400 \times 300}\right]$\\ \text{ and } \text { or, } \quad 0.$70=\frac{E_a}{19.15 \times 1200}\\ & \text { or, } \quad E_a=0.7 \times 19.15 \times 1200 \\ & =16086 \mathrm{~J} \\ & =16.08 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \\ & E_a \approx 16.10 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \\ & \end{aligned} Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.$

questions.q:
The half-life for decay of radioactive ${}^{14} \text{C}$ is 5730 years. An archaeological artefact containing wood has only 80% of the ${}^{14} \text{C}$ activity as found in living trees. The age of the artefact would be:
[Given: log 1.25 = 0.0969]
questions.solution:
Radioactive decay follows first order kinetics. $\text{L}\text{e}\text{t}{[ \text{A} ]}_{0} = 100$

$\begin{array}{ll}∴ [ \text{A} ] = 100 \times 80\text{%} = 80 \\ \text{D}\text{e}\text{c}\text{a}\text{y}\text{constant} ( \text{k} ) = \dfrac{0.693}{{t}_{1 / 2}} = \dfrac{0.693}{5730} \\ \text{t} = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \text\log\dfrac{[ \text{A}\text{o} ]}{[ \text{A} ]} \\ = \dfrac{2.303}{\dfrac{0.693}{5730}} \text\log\dfrac{100}{80} \\ = \dfrac{2.303 \times 5730}{0.693} \times \text\log1.25 \\ = \dfrac{2.303 \times 5730}{0.693} \times 0.0969 = 1 8 4 5 \text{yrs}\end{array}$

questions.q: Rate of reaction for $2 \mathrm{X}+\mathrm{Y} \rightarrow 3 \mathrm{~W}+\mathrm{Z}$ is $1.2 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{dm}^{-3} \mathrm\sec^{-1}$ when $[\mathrm{X}]=[\mathrm{Y}]=0.6 \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{dm}^{-3}$ Calculate value of rate constant if reaction is first order in $\mathrm{X}$ and zero order in Y
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{R}=-\frac{1}{2} \frac{\mathrm{d}[\mathrm{X}]}{\mathrm{dt}}=-\frac{\mathrm{d}[\mathrm{Y}]}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{1}{3} \frac{\mathrm{d}[\mathrm{W}]}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{\mathrm{d}[\mathrm{Z}]}{\mathrm{dt}} \\ & \mathrm{R}=\mathrm{k}[\mathrm{X}] \\ & 1.2 \times 10^{-4}=\mathrm{k}(0.6) \\ & \mathrm{k}=2 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{dm}^{-3} \mathrm\sec^{-1}\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
Let us consider a zero order reaction,

The energy of activation of the reaction (in $\mathrm{kJ} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ ) is

questions.q: For an elementary reaction, ${X}_{( g )} ⟶ {Y}_{( g )} + {Z}_{( g )}$, the ${t}_{1 / 2}$ is $10$ minutes. In what period of time would the concentration of $X$ be reduced to $10 %$ of its original concentration?
questions.solution:
${X}_{( g )} ⟶ {Y}_{( g )} + {Z}_{( g )}$

Let the concentration at$t = 0 = x$

The concentration after time $t = t = a - x = 10 % x = 0 . 1x$

$K = \dfrac{0 . 693}{t\dfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{0 . 693}{10} = 0 . 0693$

According to the integrated rate law,

$t = \dfrac{1}{K}ln\dfrac{a}{a - x} = \dfrac{1}{0 . 0693}ln\dfrac{1}{0 . 1} = \dfrac{1}{0 . 0693}ln10 = \dfrac{2 . 303}{0 . 0693} = 33 . 2$

Hence, the time is equal to the~$33 . 2minutes$

questions.q:
A substance undergoes a first-order decomposition. The decomposition follows two parallel first-order reactions as given below.

The percentage distributions of $B$ and $C$ are

(${k}_{1} = 1 . 26 \times {10}^{- 4}s^{- 1}$~and~${k}_{2} = 3 . 8 \times {10}^{- 5}s^{- 1}$)
questions.solution:
In the given parallel reaction, a reactant $A$ is dissociating to produce two products $B$ and $C$~simultaneously as follows,

Where~${k}_{1} = 1 . 26 \times {10}^{- 4}s^{- 1}$~and~${k}_{2} = 3 . 8 \times {10}^{- 5}s^{- 1}$

In a parallel reaction, the ratio of the concentrations of products at any time is equal to the ratio of the rate constant of their respective reactions, i.e.,

\left[B\right]\left[C\right] = \dfrac{k1}{k2}$

Then, the percentage of $B$ can be calculated as follows,

$% \left[B\right] = \dfrac{k1}{{k}_{1} + {k}_{2}} \times 100 % \left[B\right] = \dfrac{1 . 26 \times {10}^{- 4}}{1 . 26 \times {10}^{- 4} + 3 . 8 \times {10}^{- 5}} \times 100 % \left[B\right] = 76 . 83 %$

Similarly, the percentage of $C$,

$% \left[C\right] = \dfrac{k2}{{k}_{1} + {k}_{2}} \times 100 % \left[C\right] = \dfrac{3 . 8 \times {10}^{- 5}}{1 . 26 \times {10}^{- 4} + 3 . 8 \times {10}^{- 5}} \times 100 % \left[C\right] = 23 . 17 %$

Therefore, the percentage of $B$ and $C$ will be~$76 . 83 %$ and $23 . 17 %$, \text{ and } respectively.

$

For an exothermic reaction, following two steps are involved.

$\begin{cases}\text{Step 1.} & \text{A} + \text{B} \to \text{I} & & \left(\text{slow}\right) \\ \text{Step 2.} & \text{I} \to \text{AB} & & \left(\text{fast}\right)\end{cases}$

Which of the following graphs correctly represent this reaction ?
questions.solution: In any reaction mechanism the no. of activated complexes showing maxima of potential energies is the no. of steps in that mechanism and in between these maxima is a valley where lies a more stable intermediate. There is one reaction intermediate lying at valley of two maxima representing two steps. E<sub>a</sub> for first step should be higher than second step as first is slow step. These requirements fulfilled by choice (ii) & not choice (i) the choice (iv) is not possible because that is for endothermic reaction  \left(\Delta \text{H} + \text{ve}\right)$& (ii) is single step equation so not possible.$

questions.q: Rate of reaction $\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y} \rightarrow$ product is $5.4 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{dm}^{-3} \mathrm\sec^{-1}$. When $[\mathrm{x}]=0.2 \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{dm}^{-3}$ and $[\mathrm{y}]=0.1 \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{dm}^{-3}$, calculate rate constant of reaction if it is first order in $\mathrm{X}$ and second order in $\mathrm{Y}$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{r}=-\frac{\mathrm{d}(\mathrm{x})}{\mathrm{dt}}=-\frac{\mathrm{d}(\mathrm{y})}{\mathrm{dt}} \\ & \mathrm{r}=5.4 \times 10^{-2} \frac{\mathrm{mol}}{\mathrm{dm}^3-\mathrm\sec} \\ & \mathrm{r}=\mathrm{k}[\mathrm{x}] \cdot[\mathrm{y}]^2 \\ & 5.4 \times 10^{-2}=\mathrm{K}(0.2)(0.1)^2 \\ & \mathrm{~K}=27 \mathrm{~mol}^{-2} \mathrm{dm}^6 \mathrm\sec^{-1}\end{aligned}$
